task.boundary: teaching concept and test planning only; customer load, material, geometry and damage criterion unknown
task.source_policy: Lunar sampling case is provided as a deliberately different environment; do not transfer its parameters or cite it as proof of clamp performance.

method.name: 原型与假设测试
method.summary: 从高风险假设选择最小必要原型，预先定义可观察证据和下一步决策，通过实际实验学习而非把展示当验证。

sections.identity: 原型是一组围绕学习目标的表达或实验载体，可是纸面、交互、实体、仿真或服务扮演；不是固定开发阶段。本档以Stanford d.school Experiment Expedition公开介绍为设计学习来源，并用NASA确认章节区分工程用途证据。平台的假设登记、判据和停止条件为适配，不声称原型法由某一机构独创，也不复制有非商业许可限制的工作表。
sections.problem: 团队经常一开始就做精致模型，投入很大却只证明能展示；或询问用户“喜欢吗”，得到礼貌评价，没检验购买、操作、维护和技术可行性的关键假设。反过来，把早期探索做成复杂正式实验也会拖慢学习。本法先明确最危险的不确定性，再做只需足以触发真实行为或检验机理的原型，把问题、证据与下一步决策接起来。
sections.principle: 原型保真度应服务待学内容，不是越像成品越好。外观模型可测握持空间却不能证明耐久，功能台架可测机理却不能证明用户能在现场顺利操作。假设要描述对象、条件、预期行为或性能及可观察证据；探索性问题可以开放，但不能事后包装为预先定义的确认。实验前明确支持、反驳或不确定的信号，控制引导、样本偏差和混杂影响，观察与解释分开记录。低成本学习不等于低安全要求。
sections.applicability: 适合概念初期、交互细节、机构机理、服务流程及高不确定设计变化。关键是存在可检验问题，并能在可接受风险与成本下取得相关证据。若真实危险、昂贵破坏或特殊环境使原型测试不可行，应先用安全替代、分析或专家规划。成熟产品法规、承载和可靠性结论需相应工程验证；几次早期原型访谈不能替代。
sections.interpretation: 有效输出不只是修改建议，而是哪些假设受何种证据支持、哪些被反驳、哪些仍未知，下一步该继续、改向、补实验还是停止。测试失败可能来自假设错误、原型不足、任务不真实或方法偏差，应分别分析。样本少、便利招募和模拟环境应限制外推，不从少量参与者生成虚构市场比例、统计显著性或安全通过率。 引擎应按待学问题匹配原型能力，而不是按“做个原型”自动推荐高保真。为每轮保留原假设、原型版本、实际观察和改动理由，避免反复实验却无法累积知识。用户评价、行为观察与工程测量应分别存储，后续内容匹配也不能把三者当同强度证据。
sections.example: 教学演示，尚未邀请参与者：设计可单手更换的工具头。S01假设目标维修人员戴手套时能理解锁定状态，暂不测试承载。S02用分镜固定取出、装入、判断锁定的任务，选择有真实触感的低成本原型。S03预先计划观察误判、停顿和解释，不以引导问答作成功证据；锁定判据需由任务要求明确。S04在安全无载条件观察并保留原话与行为。S05若误判可能来自提示不清，记录替代解释并设计下一轮，不立即归因用户能力。S06把后续结构承载测试交工程V&V。本例没有声称任何用户已成功。 假设卡可写“对象:目标维修人员；条件:戴手套、无载安全任务；假设:能识别锁定；原型覆盖:触感/提示，不覆盖承载；信号:误判与介入；判据:待任务确认；数据:none；状态:planned”。即使做完外观模型，承载和寿命仍是不同证据任务。
sections.pitfalls: 一是先做漂亮样机再找问题，成本与学习脱节；先选关键假设。二是测试中解释答案或帮助完成，随后记“易用”；保留介入和失败。三是多个变量一起变，无法知道哪个起效；按目的隔离或明示探索。四是把模型体验好扩成产品已可量产和安全；分开证据适用域。反例：需要证实额定载荷下疲劳寿命时，纸模和用户喜好测试均不足，应转专门试验设计和验证。
sections.validation: 检查每个假设是否有对应任务、原型能力、参与者/环境、观察项和决策规则；记录招募、提示、偏差及原始材料。真实学习要实际执行，设计好的实验计划不是支持证据。对安全、人身、保密及个人数据应遵循具体任务的适当规则。若要统计推断，需要合理样本与分析方法，不能由质性观察自动升级为群体结论。
sections.adaptation: d.school公开介绍支持分镜、待测元素、制作原型、实验收数、解释与选择的循环；NASA支持预期使用、环境和用户的工程确认边界。平台将其细化为六步并添加假设优先、证据状态和正式验证接口；工作表未复制，教学工具头情境为原创。
sections.gaps: 尚无具体假设优先级、原型、真实参与者、招募与实验记录。不同原型保真度能覆盖的物理机制需项目逐项确认，不能通用推定。若后续需要统计、危险工况或认证证据，需另建合适程序、样本、工具与责任审查；本档只提供研究和学习闭环。

steps.title: 选择关键学习假设

steps.title: 把任务转为最小原型
steps.operation: 用分镜或任务流程标出待测环节，选择能表达相应行为/机理的最低必要保真度。
steps.decision: 原型未覆盖目标机理则换载体，不用外观证承载。
steps.output_description: 原型、任务和可测/不可测边界
steps.stop_condition: 测试存在未控制危险停止

steps.title: 预设观察与决策规则
steps.operation: 确定参与者环境、观察数据、提示、支持/反驳信号及下一步规则。
steps.decision: 缺合理样本只做质性学习，不承诺统计结论。
steps.output_description: 实验计划、偏差控制及判读规则
steps.stop_condition: 关键条件不能模拟则限制目标

steps.title: 实际实验并收集记录
steps.operation: 安全执行任务，记录行为、原话、条件、原型问题和研究者介入。
steps.decision: 未执行写planned，不能生成参与者反应。
steps.output_description: 原始观察、偏差和执行状态

steps.title: 解释并检查替代原因

steps.decision: 超出证据范围不外推总体、寿命或安全。

steps.decision: 没有实际数据只产计划，不宣称概念通过。

inputs.scope: Frame the bench-clamp holding and damage-prevention problem for teaching and subsequent test planning. This is a draft problem brief, not an approved requirements baseline or evidence of product performance.

conditions.text: The supplied task specifies a bench clamp and the desired outcome of holding a workpiece without damage.
Customer load, workpiece material, geometry and damage criterion are unknown; specifications and acceptance thresholds cannot yet be fixed.
The supplied lunar-sampling excerpt concerns a different environment. Its transferability is not established; its parameters and reported achievements provide no proof of bench-clamp performance.

payload.actor: Intended bench-clamp operator; customer identity, capabilities and work context are unknown.
payload.boundary: Teaching concept and test planning only; customer load, material, geometry and damage criterion unknown. Stop specification finalization until these conditions are clarified. No concept selection, physical testing or engineering validation is established.

requirements.text: The bench clamp should retain the intended workpiece during the intended operation under use conditions to be established.
requirements.acceptance: Proposed verification plan only: first establish workpiece geometry, applied loads, load directions, holding duration and allowable movement with the responsible stakeholder; then plan a retention test against those agreed conditions. No threshold or result is available.

requirements.text: Clamping and release should leave the workpiece within an agreed damage criterion.
requirements.acceptance: Proposed verification plan only: identify material, surface condition and unacceptable changes; agree inspection methods and acceptance limits before planning a before-and-after assessment. Damage criteria and results remain unknown.

conditions.text: Whether adequate retention and acceptable workpiece condition can be achieved together is unresolved for the customer's unknown use conditions.
Requirement owners, confirmation authority, priority rules and change-approval responsibilities have not been supplied. Both requirements remain draft proposals.
Proposed change process: retain requirement IDs and revision history, record the reason for each change, and revisit affected concepts and verification plans before establishing a confirmed baseline.

unknowns: Who operates the clamp, for which work operation, and in what bench environment?
What are the workpiece material, surface finish, geometry and dimensional variation?
What loads, directions, durations and allowable movements define successful holding?
What constitutes damage, and how should it be inspected or measured?
What bench interfaces, operating constraints and applicable safety requirements must be investigated?
Which requirements are hard constraints, and who can confirm them and approve changes?
What representative workpieces and verification resources would be available for a later test plan?

inputs.scope: Proposed functional model for teaching and later test planning. Maps draft REQ01 retention and REQ02 damage prevention to candidate functions and interfaces. No requirements approval, concept selection, physical feasibility or test execution is established.

conditions.text: The task requests a bench clamp that holds a workpiece without damage. Input requirements REQ01 and REQ02 remain proposed; their hardness is unknown.
Customer loads, workpiece material, geometry, allowable movement and damage criteria are unknown.
The functions, flows and scenarios below are modeling proposals. Necessity denotes their proposed contribution to the goal, not confirmed customer approval or physical feasibility.
The supplied lunar-sampling case has unestablished transferability and supplies no clamp performance evidence or customer parameters.

payload.boundary: Candidate functional boundary includes establishing workpiece contact, applying and maintaining restraint, managing contact effects, releasing restraint and assessing workpiece condition. External parties and objects are the operator or other actuation source, workpiece, bench/support and operation imposing loads; their characteristics remain unknown. Proposed normal path: establish contact, apply restraint, maintain restraint during work, release, assess condition. Proposed abnormal walkthroughs: workpiece slip, excessive contact effects, loss of actuation input and incomplete release. These are planning scenarios, not observed failures. Pause specification finalization and architecture freezing until use conditions and acceptance criteria are clarified.

functions.verb_object: Establish workpiece contact — proposed prerequisite for REQ01; accommodate the intended workpiece without selecting a jaw geometry or mechanism.
Apply restraint — proposed contribution to REQ01; transform an unspecified actuation input into workpiece restraint.
Maintain workpiece restraint — proposed contribution to REQ01 throughout the intended operation; required loads and duration remain unknown.
Manage workpiece contact effects — proposed contribution to REQ02 during engagement, holding and release; acceptable effects remain undefined.
Release workpiece restraint — proposed contribution to REQ02 during removal; release behavior and operator interaction require clarification.
Assess workpiece condition — proposed supporting activity for later verification of REQ02; allocation to an operator or inspection resource is unresolved.

flows.description: Proposed transfer of actuation work through the contact-management function during engagement. Input source, displacement, losses and magnitude are unknown; this does not establish a mechanism.
Proposed information dependency: contact readiness permits restraint application. This may be an operator judgment; no sensor or automatic interlock is specified.
Proposed information dependency: restraint establishment precedes the holding phase. How readiness is judged and what happens if it is uncertain remain unresolved.
Proposed handoff of the released workpiece for condition assessment. Inspection handling must itself be considered when defining damage assessment.

interfaces.text: Proposed workpiece interface: F01–F05 interact with the workpiece through contact and restraint. Material, finish, geometry, contact regions, force distribution, displacement and permitted surface changes are unknown. Interface owner and confirmation authority are unassigned. Proposed derived requirement: establish compatible contact conditions for retention and damage prevention before fixing a design.

Proposed actuation interface: an external operator or other source supplies input to F02 and initiates F05. Input type, magnitude, units, travel, timing, feedback and behavior after input loss are unknown. Do not presume manual, powered or continuously energized actuation.

Proposed support interface: F03 transfers reaction loads to a bench or other support. Attachment method, support stiffness, allowable movement and load directions are unknown. Later planning should define both clamp-side and support-side responsibilities and compatible limits.

Proposed operation interface: the intended work operation imposes disturbances on the restrained workpiece. Load histories, durations, directions and interaction with release are unknown. Proposed derived requirement: define when work may begin and how slip or uncertain restraint should be handled.

Proposed assessment interface: F06 receives the released workpiece and a pre-clamping condition record, and returns an assessment to the responsible reviewer. Inspection method, reference condition, acceptance limits, reviewer and record format remain unknown. This is a verification-planning dependency, not a specified built-in sensing function.

Proposed verification plan: after stakeholders define representative workpieces, load conditions, allowable movement and damage criteria, plan retention observation and before/after condition assessment. Review engagement, holding, release and abnormal scenarios together. No procedure, threshold, sample count or acceptance result is established.

unknowns: Which work operation, operator capabilities and bench environment define the operating scenario?
What workpiece materials, finishes, geometries and variations must be accommodated?
What loads, directions, durations and allowable movements define retention?
What constitutes damage during engagement, holding, release and inspection?
Can retention and damage prevention be achieved together under the eventual use conditions?
What actuation source, support interface and release behavior are required?
What are the consequences and required responses for slip, excessive contact effects, input loss or incomplete release?
Who owns and confirms each requirement and interface, and which constraints are hard? Hardness remains unknown.
How should functions be allocated among clamp, operator and external assessment resources? No physical architecture is selected.
What verification resources and representative workpieces will be available? All verification described here remains a plan.

inputs.scope: Teaching concept enumeration and verification planning for a bench clamp intended to hold a workpiece without damage. Uses the supplied proposed functional model and morphological-analysis method. All implementation principles below are teaching hypotheses, not customer requirements or demonstrated solutions. No preferred concept, approved specification, prototype execution or engineering validation is established. The lunar-sampling case supplies no clamp performance evidence and contributes no parameters to these concepts.

conditions.text: The task specifies a bench clamp and the desired outcome of holding a workpiece without damage.
Customer loads, workpiece material, geometry, allowable movement and damage criteria remain unknown. REQ01 and REQ02 remain proposed; their hardness is unknown.

F01 establishes contact; F02 applies restraint; F03 maintains restraint; F04 manages contact effects; F05 releases restraint; F06 assesses workpiece condition. These allocations remain modeling proposals from the supplied FunctionModel.
Manual input, pneumatic supply, fixed-reference contact and external inspection are alternative teaching assumptions. None is established as available or acceptable for the customer.
The proposed contact-management option is a hypothesis to investigate; distributing contact does not by itself establish adequate retention or freedom from damage.

options.principle: Establish workpiece contact against a fixed reference before applying restraint.
conditions: Teaching hypothesis derived from the method example.
Requires compatible workpiece geometry, accessible contact regions and a reaction path to the support; all remain unknown.

options.principle: Convert manual rotation through a screw transmission into closing displacement and restraint.
conditions: Manual operation is an assumption, not a customer constraint.
Operator input, travel, transmission geometry and resulting contact forces require definition.

options.principle: Use a pneumatic cylinder to produce closing displacement and restraint.
conditions: Pneumatic supply availability and acceptability are unknown.
For the exclusion example only, assume a single-direction closing cylinder with no screw transmission.
Pressure, stroke, control and support interfaces remain unspecified.

options.principle: Investigate retaining the screw position through transmission resistance after manual input stops.
conditions: Position retention is a hypothesis, not an established self-locking property.
Requires review of transmission geometry, friction, disturbances, load duration and support reactions.

options.principle: Investigate maintaining restraint through sustained pneumatic input.
conditions: Continuous supply and control are assumed for this teaching route.
Leakage, supply loss, movement and required holding duration remain unresolved.

options.principle: Investigate distributing restraint over a defined contact region to manage local workpiece effects.
conditions: Proposed interpretation of F04, not an evidenced damage-prevention solution.
Contact area, material, surface interaction and deformation require definition.
Any effect on slip resistance must be evaluated together with damage.

options.principle: Reverse the same screw transmission to withdraw contact and release restraint.
conditions: Requires an actual reversible screw transmission connected to the moving contact.
Release travel, residual contact and removal clearance remain unknown.

options.principle: Investigate elastic return after pneumatic closing input is removed.
conditions: Requires a return element and a defined pressure-release path.
Return force, sticking, release travel and behavior during unintended supply loss remain unknown.
Compatibility with sustained holding must be investigated.

options.principle: Allocate before-and-after workpiece condition assessment to an external operator or inspection resource.
conditions: Supporting verification activity rather than a specified built-in sensing mechanism.
Requires an agreed reference condition, damage criterion, inspection method and responsible reviewer.
No assessment has been performed.

combinations.reason: Manual screw route covers all six proposed functions: reference contact, screw closing, hypothesized position retention, contact management, reverse-screw release and external assessment. The screw supplies a conceptual connection between closing and release, but holding behavior, contact effects and bench reactions remain unknown. Manual operation and reverse travel introduce operator and clearance dependencies. Retained for investigation only; no recommendation is supported.

Pneumatic route covers all six proposed functions through reference contact, pneumatic closing, sustained input, contact management, elastic return and external assessment. It adds supply, control and return-element dependencies. Whether pressure can maintain restraint while permitting intentional release, including behavior after supply loss, remains unresolved. No recommendation is supported.

Under the explicit O03 topology assumption of a closing cylinder without a screw transmission, O07 cannot release restraint by reversing that absent transmission. This is a conditional logical conflict, not an empirical performance judgment. Adding a screw would require a newly defined option and combination.

compatibility.reason: At the stated principle level only, forward and reverse operation refer to the same reversible screw transmission. This conditional connection establishes neither release clearance nor overall feasibility.
Screw-driven closing does not establish that position or restraint will persist after input stops; transmission and disturbance conditions are missing.
O03 explicitly excludes a screw transmission for this topology, whereas O07 requires that transmission as the release mechanism.
Closing, sustained holding and elastic return require a coordinated pressure and motion sequence. Available supply, intentional venting, return force and input-loss behavior are undefined.

Whole-route check for M01 remains open: contact geometry, force transmission, restraint persistence, support reactions, release and assessment must jointly satisfy retention and damage criteria that are not yet defined.

Whole-route check for M02 remains open: supply and return behavior interact with contact forces, restraint continuity, support reactions and damage. Pairwise consistency cannot resolve these system interactions.

unknowns: Confirm the intended operation, operator capabilities and available actuation resources before comparing manual and pneumatic routes.
Obtain workpiece materials, finishes, geometries and variation; then plan contact and clearance review for engagement, holding and release.
Establish loads, directions, duration and allowable movement; then plan restraint and bench-reaction analysis for each retained route.
Agree damage criteria and inspection methods with the responsible stakeholder before planning before-and-after assessment.
Investigate whether retention and acceptable contact effects can coexist; no acceptable force range has been established.
For M01, plan review of screw position retention, disturbance sensitivity and release behavior once transmission and load conditions are available.
For M02, define the supply, control and return sequence; then plan walkthroughs of intentional release, supply loss and incomplete release.
Identify requirement owners, confirmation authority and hard constraints. Unknown hard gates prevent recommendation or unique selection.

No approved comparison baseline exists. After requirements are clarified, use the same workpiece, load, movement and damage criteria for both routes; compare operator effort, resource dependence and interface complexity without inventing scores.

Prototype and verification activities remain proposals only. Define representative workpieces, resources, procedures and acceptance limits before any later execution; no tests, measurements or acceptance results are supplied.

inputs.scope: Teaching comparison frame and test-planning record only. M01 is a provisional datum, not an approved or demonstrated clamp. Performance comparisons stop because retention conditions and damage criteria are undefined. No concept is recommended, tested or engineering validated.

conditions.text: The supplied task seeks a bench clamp that holds a workpiece without damage. REQ01 and REQ02 remain proposed; customer requirement hardness remains unknown.
Use M01, the manual screw route, as a provisional teaching datum and compare M02, the pneumatic route. This datum choice is a planning assumption, not a customer preference.
The Boolean hard field below describes a proposed procedural gate for permitting selection, not the unknown hardness of customer requirements. Unknown customer hardness is not represented as false.

M03 remains conditionally excluded under its supplied topology: its release option requires a screw transmission that its closing option explicitly omits. This logical conflict establishes no performance result for M01 or M02.
The lunar-sampling excerpt has unestablished transferability and supplies neither customer clamp parameters nor evidence of clamp performance.

criteria.text: Proposed selection-readiness gate: establish applicable constraints and demonstrate retention and acceptable workpiece condition against stakeholder-defined use conditions before recommending a route. This procedural gate does not assign hardness to REQ01 or REQ02.

judgments.basis: Record author: planning assessment from supplied inputs only. Datum designation does not establish gate passage. Loads, material, geometry, allowable movement, damage limits and requirement authority remain unknown; no evidence establishes retention or acceptable workpiece condition for M01.

Record author: planning assessment from supplied inputs only. Loads, material, geometry, allowable movement, damage limits and requirement authority are unknown. Neither M02 nor datum M01 has evidence establishing this gate. Their shared contact-management option does not establish equivalent damage or retention performance. No relative performance score is justified.

sensitivity: Datum choice cannot resolve missing acceptance criteria. Switching the datum to M02 would leave selection readiness unknown.

M01 assumes manual input and hypothesized screw-position retention; M02 assumes pneumatic supply, sustained input and elastic return. Resource availability and acceptable input-loss behavior could change which routes merit further investigation.
Contact geometry, material and surface interaction could change retention and damage together. No ranking, weights or symbol totals are justified.
unknowns: Confirm the intended work operation, operator capabilities, bench interface and available actuation resources.
Define representative workpiece materials, finishes, geometries and variation.
Establish loads, directions, holding duration and allowable movement; agree what constitutes damage and how it will be assessed.
Identify requirement owners and confirmation authority; determine customer requirement hardness without treating the proposed procedural gate as approval.

After criteria are defined, plan comparisons under common workpiece and loading conditions, including engagement, holding, release and before-and-after condition assessment. Procedures, thresholds, sample counts and resources remain to be defined; nothing has been executed.

For M01, plan investigation of restraint persistence, disturbance sensitivity and reverse-screw release. For M02, plan investigation of sustained supply, intentional venting, return behavior and supply loss.
Reopen the Pugh performance matrix only after its criteria and supporting evidence are sufficiently defined. Retain both routes as unresolved teaching hypotheses, without a preferred concept.

{
"year": 2025,
"name": "嫦娥五/六号月球钻取采样方法及系统设计",
"unit": "哈尔滨工业大学,北京圣视环宇科技有限公司",
"participants": "姜生元,张伟伟,唐钧跃,范继五,全齐全,侯绪研,阮旭,杨暄昊,杜坤,汪凌昕",
"number": "12025070107",
"desc": "探月工程三期嫦娥五/六号任务的核心使命是月球无人自主采样返回。带有地质层序信息的深层月壤样品，能为月球成因和演化历史、资源赋存和可用性研究提供直接证据。钻取采样是获取深层保层序月壤样品的最有效手段。探月工程三期是我国首次地外天体采样返回任务，面临月壤及剖面特性非确知、月面环境极端、探测器重量/功耗/包络尺度约束苛刻、地月通信时延大等挑战。\n自2011年起，项目组承研月球钻取采样国家任务，提出了面向月球采样设计理论与准则，首创了月球“钻-表-封”采样总体设计方案，攻克了月球钻取系统集成设计、地-月协同智能操控系统设计、月球钻取拟实验证装备设计难题，参与研制了嫦娥五/六号月球钻取系统型号产品，圆满完成了中国首次月球正面钻取采样任务(2020年)、世界首次月球背面钻取采样任务(2024年)。\n1、首次提出颗粒适应性钻具设计、大尺度连续保层序取样、相似性/等效性/覆盖性等设计理念，制定了动力裕度设计、可靠性优先、有限目标保证等设计准则，解决了我国首次月球采样任务系统设计无依据的难题。\n2、首创了月球“钻-表-封”无人采样总体设计方案，构建了月球采样作业场景，突破了钻取系统与探测器构型布局、动作节拍以及参数匹配设计难题，国际首次实现了一次任务同时获取表层和深层两类月壤样品。\n3、提出了双管单袋内翻包覆无滑差钻取和样品收纳新方法，设计了双管单袋无滑差钻取采样机构，实现了非确知深层月壤的高适应钻进与保层序取样，在机理上解决了传统取样方法因力链卡滞
